question.text: Ms. Ananya Bose is a senior analyst at the Investment Manager of Himalaya Growth AIF (Cat II). She wants to invest her own savings into the fund alongside external LPs. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum investment amount applicable to her?

answer.text: INR 25 lakhs — the concessional minimum for employees/directors of the AIF or of the Manager
INR 1 crore — the standard minimum for all AIF investors
INR 10 lakhs — the accredited investor minimum
No minimum — employees of the Manager are exempt from any threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the standard minimum investment in an AIF is INR 1 crore per investor. However, for employees or directors of the AIF or of the Manager, the minimum is reduced to INR 25 lakhs. This concession recognises that staff alignment investments strengthen GP-LP alignment but shouldn't require them to commit the same ticket as external HNIs. The Trap: INR 1 crore ignores the employee concession. INR 10 lakhs fabricates a number (AI minimums can be lower for certain products, but this isn't the employee floor). The 'no minimum' option wrongly eliminates the floor entirely. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same thresholds. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests the INR 1 crore standard. Angel Fund has NO minimum for angel investors (separate rule under Chapter 3 of the PDF). Manager's Pro-Tip: When you onboard a senior hire, plan their INR 25 lakh commitment as part of the offer letter — it's a strong alignment signal to LPs and to the hire. Document the employee-minimum usage in the PPM's investor-class table.
